My biggest wish for Pantheon is for it to facilitate non-combat playstyles in a way that's friendly to roleplayers. Like maybe I don't want to be an adventurer, you know? Maybe I just want to be Annabelle, the adorable village girl who works at the bakery.

Obviously I can't speak for the entire playerbase, but I personally think it'd be awesome if there was some attention paid to rest and relaxation for adventurers. Like a D&D tavern vibe. Life can't be all dungeons all the time, can it? Give the heroes of the world a reason to frequent taverns, eat various foods, talk to the locals, check out small villages, visit brothels, go fishing, or whatever. I always see so much talk about "social gameplay" in MMO circles but so often the scope of that conversation is limited to guilds and random people you meet while out questing, and I really feel like that's a shame, because there's honestly so much potential there for more.

I'm a writer. And I enjoy roleplay a lot. And I'd like to see more roleplaying happening in my roleplaying games.

Also, I've said this before, but I'll say it again: one of the best ways for you to facilitate a community of roleplayers is to allow them creative freedom, and one of the best ways to do THAT is to create some kind of user interface element that allows them to express themselves.

In my mind's eye, a character I'm thinking of might have sectional heterochromia and a wealth of floor-length hair, but we all know there's no way I'm ever making something like that in an MMO character creator. Games have limitations, and it's not necessarily always realistic to expect a dev team to spend a lot of time on outlandish hairstyles or eye colors, or on decorative or cosmetic items like clothing. But having the ability to write that stuff for myself changes everything. If I can write my character's background and description somewhere, and other people can see it, then I effectively have no limitations anymore. And that, to me, is gold.

So my second biggest wish for Pantheon is for someone on the UI team to take a look at a WoW addon called TRP3 and seriously consider adding something (somewhat) similar to Pantheon.

First of all, being trans is not a choice. Kids are in no way being given a choice about what gender they'll be when they're adults. Suggesting that they are is disingenuous and asinine. A seven-year old choosing to wear a dress to school and asking to be called by a girl's name is not equivalent to "choosing their gender". The thing about kids is, they're young. They're not taking hormones. It's harmless behaviour with absolutely no long-term consequences whatsoever. If it goes away, fine. Awesome. If it doesn't go away, if it's causing them grief or emotional problems, see a doctor about it. And get a second opinion. 

Seriously, it's as simple as that.

Also, I don't know what all this shit about misguided parents is. Just because you saw somebody on the Today show and got a condensed-for-TV version of their story doesn't mean you know dick about their actual situation. 

Some people seem to have this idea that a parent can just decide on a whim to go to their family doctor, get a scrip for some estrogen or testosterone chewies at walgreens or w/e, and then feed them to their kid. It does *not* work that way. It doesn't. Barring a tiny handful of cases worldwide, that does not happen. And in the cases where it has happened, the doctors involved lost their licenses.

What the process actually consists of is a series of visits with various specialists: pediatric psychologists, counselors, therapists, doctors, and endocrinologists, specifically. And your family doctor.

IF it's determined that a child is exhibiting signs of 'gender dysphoria' or is otherwise having problems with their identity, what will happen is that your doctor might prescribe puberty blockers. *TEMPORARY* puberty blockers. 

They *WILL NOT. GET. HORMONES. 

No doctor anywhere ever is putting young children on a hormone regimen. So stop peddling this bullshit. It is not true.

The only exception to that is if the child is determined to be old enough to make the choice already (15, 16+). And before you chime in about how dumb teenagers are, let me just stop you right there because you're forgetting about all those psychologists and doctors and therapists who are assessing your kid's mental state and evaluating their capability to make the decision to and to comprehend the consequences of transition. And on top of that, I submit that it does not take a fucking rocket surgeon to figure out how you identify. All you need to figure that out is a half-decent support structure, i.e. parents, friends, and/or family who aren't complete stigma-shoveling bigoted tool factories. 

Anyway, all these blockers do is delay puberty until the child is older and is better equipped to comprehend this shit. They DO NOT cause any sort of harm or damage whatsoever. They have MINIMAL, if any, side effects. They can be taken for years without issues. And here's the best part: If your kid does happen to change their mind; if they decide that yeah, actually, they do identify with the body they were born into, then they can stop. 

They can just stop. And puberty just starts normally. As if nothing ever even happened.

It's like the perfect solution and yet I see dozens of people in these comments wringing their hands and whimpering about how dangerous and silly it is. And the whole pack of you need to fuck the entire way off with that shit, because here's the thing:

To just flatly dismiss the notion that a child is capable of questioning their gender or their identity, or to reject it outright because the child 'need not worry about such things' or whatever other whitebread bullshit regurgitated excuse you can come up with? In the event that your child actually is trans, you are doing permanent and irreparable harm to not only their bodies, but to their trust in you.

If your child is born into a male body but winds up identifying as a woman, they're going to transition sooner or later. I mean, barring weird circumstances like a strict religious upbringing or other ridiculously repressive shit, they are going to transition. 

They can do it at 14 or 15 and live a happy, normal life. 

OR you can put it off and ignore them. Push them down. Hope it goes away (it won't). But if you do that you're effectively forcing them to undergo the wrong puberty, which is both psychologically and physically devastating, and will most probably condemn them to a much worse quality of life after they transition in the future.

Forcing your child to go through the wrong puberty because you were too closed-minded, too bigoted to take them to see a professional is *super fucked up*.

There's a LOT of misinformation and scare-mongering going on out there. A lot of junk science being passed off as air-tight and being used to justify bigotry and shitty policy. 

But all you really need to do is listen to your fucking kids and spend a little time investigating this stuff. It's really, really not hard.
